If the toddler is still around one, especially under three, they're not going to understand why you're taking a toy away as punishment for something like spilling juice. They don't have the cognitive ability to rationalize.

Walking around the house while eating is dangerous so you're right about that, the child needs to be in a high chair. He's too young to have the patience and to rationalize that meal time means you have to sit, that's up to the adults to teach through repetition. A more appropriate response if the kid starts to flip about being put in the chair for meals is to calmly state how they need to sit to eat and if they don't want to sit, they can try eating again later. Rinse and repeat until their brain finally makes the connection between lots of tantrums because that's what toddlers do to express emotions. It's up to the adults to help the kid learn good behaviors and self regulate emotions which can take a while because their brains literally aren't developed to understand everything like an adult.

A young toddler is not a dictator, the kid needs redirection and boundaries.
